column1: # Every in-tree construction that makes an error AMBIGUOUS, one per line, for
#   file <TAB> a pattern unique to that construction <TAB> modules to test
# The pattern is matched literally and must select exactly one line, so the
# inventory survives edits above it; pinsweep reports NO-MUTATION rather than
# guessing if a pattern goes stale or becomes ambiguous.
# The modules column is what limits the sweep: a rule pinned only from a module
# not listed here reads UNPINNED.  drivers/kafka is the known cross-module
# case -- its rules are asserted by drivers/kafka/kafkago's cross-driver table
# -- so both are listed for it.
# The two `out[i].Ambiguous = true` rows are COMPOSED ambiguity: a transformer
# copies a whole rule set and adds the flag, so their verdict covers the copied
# set as a whole rather than one rule.

column2: Code: CodeAmbiguous, Ambiguous: true, Err: unattributedCause{err},
Code: mq.CodeSettlementUnknown, Ambiguous: true, Err: cause}
Code: mq.CodeClosed, Ambiguous: true, Err: errClosedUnanswered
Code:  mq.CodeUnavailable, Retryable: true, Ambiguous: true,

column1: # ---- drivers/kafka (franz-go); its cross-driver pin lives in kafkago ----

column2: Code: mq.CodeSettlementUnknown, Retryable: false, Ambiguous: true,
Code: mq.CodeAmbiguous, Retryable: false, Ambiguous: true, Err: err,
Code: mq.CodeDeadlineExceeded, Retryable: false, Ambiguous: true,

column1: # driverkit's generic mapper builds an *OpError from whatever Rule matched, so
# flipping Retryable here flips EVERY rule in every driver at once. It is
# plumbing, not a construction with a flag of its own.

column3: Rule{Code: code, Retryable: retryable, Ambiguous: ambiguous}
